claims: Theorem 1.1: for every integer k >= 2, every family of N unit squares in [0,k]^2 that are pairwise disjoint as closed sets has k^2 - N >= kappa log k with kappa = 0.033 (natural logarithm), and k^2 - N >= (0.99977 log k + 0.3819)/30.147 for k >= 10^13 (paper/paper.tex, Theorem 1.1)

Corollary 1.2: c*(k) := max{c : s(k^2 - c) = k} >= kappa log k - 1, so for every fixed c, s(k^2 - c) = k for all sufficiently large k; for c = 4 the second bound gives s(k^2 - 4) = k for log k > 120.24 (Corollary 1.2, Remark 7.4)
Without the computer-assisted Lemma 4.10 (K_w* = 9), the analytic Lemma 4.9 (K_w = 13) gives kappa = 0.027 (Remark 7.5)

Lemma 4.10: at an uncovered point at most 9 Roth-Vaughan rectangles of nearly touching pairs overlap, by a branch-and-bound cover of 78,673 accepted boxes (data/kw9_data.zip), each re-verified in Arb ball arithmetic by code/verify_leaves2.py with 59,238 further bisections, largest rigorous bound 9, no failure; the cover's completeness checked by code/coverage_check.py and by two independent programs in code/coverage_independent/
